chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed ibn Khaleefa, who said:

There was by the side of my house a basket containing two eggs from the doves of the Haram. The boy went to overturn the basket, not knowing that there were two eggs in it, so he broke them. I went out and met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and mentioned that to him, so he said: 'Give in charity two handfuls of fine flour.'

He said: Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) afterwards and informed him, so he said: 'The price of two birds, to feed the doves of the Haram with it.' I met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and informed him, so he said: 'He spoke the truth. Narrate with it, for rather, he took it from his forefathers.'

key_terms.آبَائِهِ: His forefathers (referring to the Imams' lineage)
key_terms.حَمَامُ الْحَرَمِ: The sacred doves of the Haram (Mecca/Medina)
key_terms.صَدَقَكَ: He spoke the truth / He is correct
key_terms.مِكْتَلٌ: A basket or container for holding grain or eggs

ai.seo_question: What is the correct expiation for accidentally killing a sacred dove of the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'daman' (compensation) for accidental damage, specifically distinguishing between the value of the animal and the specific act of feeding the sacred birds of the Haram. The validation by Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, who traced the ruling to the Imams' forefathers, highlights the continuity of oral tradition and the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in refining legal precedents. It underscores the sanctity of the Haram's ecosystem and the precise monetary or material compensation required for unintentional transgressions within its boundaries.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed Bin Khaleefa who said,

‘By the side of my house there is a nest where were two eggs from a dove of the Al-Harram. So the boy went and threw the nest and he did not know that there were two eggs in it. So he broke them both. So I went out and met Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan and mentioned that to him, so he said, ‘Give in charity with two handfuls of flour’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then I met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> afterwards, so I informed him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The price of the two birds to feed the doves of the Al-Harram with it’. So I met Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan and informed him, so he said, ‘You speak the truth. Narrate with it, for rather, he<sup>asws</sup> has taken it from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Yazid ibn Khalifah who has said the following:

“In one side of my house there were two eggs of pigeon of al-Haram (the sacred area). The boy went to move the cluster not knowing that the eggs were there and he broke them. I went out and met ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hassan and mentioned it to him. He said, ‘You must give charity of two handful of flour.’

I then met abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and informed him (the Imam) about it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Pay the price of two birds as feed for the pigeon of al-Haram (the sacred area).’ I then met ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hassan and informed him about it and he said, ‘He (the Imam) has told you the truth. You can narrate it because he (the Imam) has taken it from his ancestors.’”
